about: `single_dash_long` lets a single-dash token name a long flag, as getopt_long_only(3) and GNU ld read it: the whole name is tried as a long first, and only a token that names no long falls back to the short-flag rules, bundles included.

vectors.doc: `-shared` names the long `--shared`.
The double-dash spelling still binds.
`-soname=libfoo.so` binds the text after the first `=`, as the double-dash form does.
`-soname libfoo.so` takes the following token.
`-lfoo` names no long, so it is the short `-l` with the attached value `foo`.
A long name wins over a short with an attached value: `-export-dynamic` is the long, `-emain` is `-e main`.
Names match exactly, never as a prefix: `-Ttext=0x1000` is the long `--Ttext`, while `-Tlink.ld` is `-T link.ld`.
A flag declared `single_dash_long=#false` needs `--`, which is how GNU ld keeps `-omagic` meaning `-o magic`.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
flag "-o --output <file>"
flag "--omagic" single_dash_long=#false

vectors.doc: The opted-out flag still binds with two dashes.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
flag "-o --output <file>"
flag "--omagic" single_dash_long=#false

vectors.doc: A token that names no long is read by the short-flag rules, so `-sx` is still a bundle.
A negated spelling is a long too: `-no-as-needed` turns `--as-needed` off.
A single-dash token that names neither a long nor a bundle is an unrecognized flag, as it is without the setting.
A word owed to a flag as its value is not a token of its own, so `-mllvm -shared` gives `mllvm` the value `-shared` rather than respelling it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
flag "--mllvm <opt>" allow_hyphen_values=#true
flag "--shared"

vectors.doc: A single-dash long is flag-like, so it ends a variadic flag's run and binds.
After `--` a single-dash token is a value like any other.
Without the setting a single-dash token is only ever short flags, so `-shared` names nothing.
A flag's own `single_dash_long` refuses one dash where its command allows it, and grants nothing where the command said nothing.
The setting reaches subcommands, like `unknown_flags`.
A command may turn the inherited setting off for its own tokens.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
unknown_flags "error"
cmd "strict" single_dash_long=#false {
  flag "--shared"
}

vectors.doc: An inherited global long is reachable with one dash below the command that declares it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
flag "--verbose" global=#true
cmd "link"

vectors.doc: The default-subcommand lookahead reads a single-dash long as one, so `-shared` routes into the command that declares it, as `--shared` does.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
flag "-s --strip"
cmd "run" {
  flag "--shared"
  arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: A single-dash long at the default-subcommand boundary is one flag, so its letters are not read as the parent's shorts.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
args_conflicts_with_subcommands #true
flag "-s --strip"
cmd "run" {
  flag "--shared"
  arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: A root long spelled with one dash binds before a subcommand word, even though descending drops it from the flags in scope.
The same for a value-taking long: `-jobs 4 child` keeps the value with the flag.
A declared long named `1` is what `-1` names, as an exact declared short outranks the numeric shape.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
flag "--1"
arg "[n]" allow_negative_numbers=#true

vectors.doc: Where a default subcommand refuses one dash, a token naming only its long is not routed to it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
single_dash_long #true
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
unknown_flags "error"
flag "-s --strip"
cmd "run" single_dash_long=#false {
  flag "--shared"
  arg "[args]..."
}
